lesson.title: Chặng 6: Nền tảng frontend với HTML, CSS, JavaScript và TypeScript

learning_objectives.statement: Build and document a semantic browser expense page with safe DOM, storage, fetch, and TypeScript boundaries using the Stage 05 API contract.
Record actual responsive, fetch-state, runtime-validation, and error observations while distinguishing unavailable and unverified work.

activity.title: Stage 06 browser frontend, DOM, fetch, and TypeScript evidence
activity.instructions:
This bounded activity maps to DotNet-React-Roadmap/6.md. Complete Stage 05
first so the API contract and endpoint behavior are known; this activity is
a learner-attestation task, not a full Stage 06 gate.

Work in a learner-owned scratch frontend and use only learning data. Record
the actual Node/npm versions, local server origin, and API origin without
recording secrets. TypeScript must be built/transpiled before browser use;
if tooling or a browser is unavailable, record the blocker and leave the
corresponding evidence incomplete.

Build a semantic expense page with header/main/section/form, associated
labels, inputs, notification area, list/table, and total. Record a keyboard
submit and an empty/invalid form observation. Use Flexbox/Grid and a media
query for layout; inspect 320px, 768px, and a wide viewport and record what
actually changes. Treat breakpoints as design choices, not universal rules.

Implement DOM event handling with explicit element/null checks, FormData,
createElement, and textContent for user data. Record one submit flow and one
missing-element or invalid-input boundary. Do not use innerHTML with
untrusted values. Keep modules separate and exercise localStorage with
JSON.stringify/JSON.parse, missing-key, and malformed-JSON handling; do not
place tokens or other sensitive data in localStorage.

Connect fetch to the Stage 05 API. Record actual loading, success, empty,
error, 404, network/abort, and malformed-response behavior where exercised.
Remember that fetch resolves for HTTP 404/500 and rejects for network,
abort, or URL/CORS failures; read a response body once. Configure CORS or a
proxy explicitly and record the chosen origin boundary.

Define TypeScript request/response types using categoryId for requests and
categoryName for responses. Add runtime checks for unknown JSON before using
it; interfaces and type assertions do not validate server data. Record the
actual type/build command and result only if run. Keep a short README with
real run instructions and a table of observed outcomes; do not invent any.

A recorded blocker preserves an honest incomplete result; it does not earn the point for the corresponding unperformed observation. Complete each positive rubric item only with actual evidence.

Before the DOM work, exercise array map/filter/reduce on the expense data. Record expected versus observed totals for an empty array and zero-valued amounts, and one filter/sort case without mutating the original data unexpectedly.
activity.expected_output: A learner evidence note with semantic markup/keyboard and responsive observations, DOM and localStorage boundary records, actual fetch state/error observations, runtime JSON validation, TypeScript build evidence, and explicit blockers.

rubric.evidence: The note identifies semantic form/list structure, keyboard interaction, associated labels, and observed layout behavior at the chosen viewport widths. Missing or blocked required evidence remains incomplete and earns no point.

The note records null checks, safe text rendering, module boundaries, and actual missing/malformed localStorage behavior without storing secrets. It also records actual array transformation checks, including empty/zero totals and a filter/sort boundary. Missing or blocked required evidence remains incomplete and earns no point.

The note records real fetch loading/success/empty/error observations, distinguishes HTTP responses from rejected requests, and shows runtime checks for unknown JSON plus the shared categoryId/categoryName contract. Missing or blocked required evidence remains incomplete and earns no point.

The note records actual versions/build or server commands and outcomes, preserves failures as incomplete, and does not claim browser or API behavior that was not observed. Missing or blocked required evidence remains incomplete and earns no point.
